title: Flaky Pie Dough
source: Stella Parks (BraveTart), No-Stress Pie Dough, via The Splendid Table

items.body: Sift the flour through the fine strainer into a medium bowl. Whisk in the sugar and salt.
Add the butter to the flour and toss to coat, pulling apart any cubes that stick together. Pinch each cube flat, ≈¼ in thick. Don’t work it in any further: the flat pieces make the flaky layers.
Pour in all the water at once and stir with the rubber spatula. Then press and knead it in the bowl just until it forms a shaggy ball. It should look rough. Don’t add more water.
On a well-floured counter, roll the dough into a ≈10 × 15 in rectangle. If the butter turns soft and sticky at any point, refrigerate the dough 15 min, then carry on.

Fold both short ends in to meet in the middle, then close it like a book. Fold that in half, then cut it into 2 equal pieces. Wrap one tightly in plastic and refrigerate up to 2 days, or freeze up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge.

On a floured counter, roll the other piece into a 14 in round, ⅛–¼ in thick. Lay it in the pie plate and ease it into the corners without stretching. Trim to a 1¼ in overhang, fold the overhang under, and press it into a ¾ in border on the rim. Crimp with your fingers or a fork.
Cover the shell with plastic and refrigerate at least 2 h, or overnight.

Rack in the lower-middle, oven to 350 °F (177 °C). Line the cold shell with a 16 in square of foil (not parchment), pressing it into the corners, and fill it to the brim with sugar. Set it on the half sheet pan.
Bake until the crust is cooked through and lightly browned, ≈1 h. Check the bottom through the glass: it should be golden, not pale.
Lift out the foil and sugar together with both hands and set them on a plate. Once the sugar cools, keep it for baking. Cool the shell on a rack and fill it within 12 h.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: SR Legacy (sugar, unsalted butter) and Branded Foods labels (King Arthur All-Purpose, Morton). Per serving is one crust. Water, the sugar used for weighting and the flour for the counter not counted.
notes: Equal weights of butter and flour, all the water at once, and a quick roll and fold for layers, so there’s no squeeze test to over-water. Serious Eats says the folds keep it from turning “leathery and dense”. Parks bakes low and slow so it shrinks less.
Parks prefers Gold Medal bleached flour for tenderness. The numbers are for King Arthur all-purpose. Her 1¼ tsp Diamond Crystal is ¾ tsp Morton by weight.
One glass plate, so one shell at a time. The second piece makes the next pie.
